value.heading: About the team
value.text: Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.

value.heading: What you’ll do
value.text: As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains. Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.

value.heading: Responsibilities
value.text: Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.

value.heading: Responsibilities
value.text: FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints.

value.heading: Responsibilities
value.text: Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows.

value.heading: Responsibilities
value.text: Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security.

value.heading: Responsibilities
value.text: Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls.

value.heading: About Pinterest:
value.text: Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.

value.heading: About Pinterest:
value.text: Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.

value.heading: About Pinterest:
value.text: At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.

value.heading: About Pinterest:
value.text: Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here.

value.heading: About Pinterest:
value.text: With more than 640 million users around the world and 300 billion ideas saved, Pinterest Machine Learning engineers help build personalized experiences to help Pinners create a life they love. At Pinterest, you’ll experience hands-on access to an incredible vault of data and contribute large-scale recommendation systems in ways you won’t find anywhere else.

value.heading: About Pinterest:
value.text: By applying to this role, you will be considered for multiple roles open across our various ML teams. Please only apply once within the USA or Canada as multiple applications may delay our recruitment process.

value.heading: About Pinterest:
value.text: This is a general posting for multiple roles open across our various ML teams. You will have the opportunity to work on a very large scope of problems in recommender systems, search, ads, ranking, natural language processing, graph representation learning, personalization, etc.

value.heading: About Pinterest:
value.text: As a Machine Learning Engineer at Pinterest, you’ll work on tackling new challenges in machine learning and artificial intelligence. As you kickstart your career at Pinterest, you’ll join our engineering teams as we maneuver through exponential growth and massive scale while building awesome products and features, creating visually rich experiences, spearheading the discovery problem, and pinpointing tomorrow’s engineering challenges.

value.heading: What you’ll do:
value.text: Contribute to cutting-edge research in machine learning and artificial intelligence that can be applied to Pinterest problems

value.heading: What you’ll do:
value.text: Collect, analyze, and synthesize findings from data and build intelligent data-driven model

value.heading: What you’ll do:
value.text: Write clean, efficient, and sustainable code

value.heading: What you’ll do:
value.text: Use machine learning, natural language processing, and graph analysis to solve modeling and ranking problems across discovery, ads and search

value.heading: What you’ll do:
value.text: Design, build, and test models to predict engagement for notifications (push, emails, in-app notifications)

value.heading: What you’ll do:
value.text: Build content recommendation systems to power our push, email, and in-app notifications

value.heading: What you’ll do:
value.text: Work on state-of-the-art large-scale applied machine learning projects

value.heading: What you’ll do:
value.text: Scope and independently solve moderately complex problems

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: PhD in Computer Science, ML, NLP, Statistics, Information Sciences or related field required

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: Machine Learning experience (ranking, computer vision, NLP, content recommendations, embedding, information retrieval etc)

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: Experience with big data technologies (e.g., Hadoop/Spark) and scalable realtime systems that process stream data

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: Mastery of at least one systems languages (Java, C++, Python) or one ML framework (Tensorflow, Pytorch, MLFlow)

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: Proficiency with AI-native engineering, including the design of agent-friendly codebases.

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: High degree of autonomy in learning new agent-first development tools.

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: Strong critical thinking when working with AI-generated suggestions, with a clear approach to validating correctness, performance, security, and maintainability.

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: Comfort iterating on prompts, refining workflows, and adapting AI-assisted approaches based on the problem, context, and constraints.

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: Experience in research and in solving analytical problems

value.heading: What we’re looking for:
value.text: Strong communicator and team player. Being able to find solutions for open-ended problems.

value.heading: - Preferred Qualifications:
value.text: Publications in machine learning, AI, data science, data analytics, statistics, or related technical fields

value.heading: - Preferred Qualifications:
value.text: Interest in research and in applying ML to impactful real-world problems on the Pinterest product

cannot_verify: Whether this employer will sponsor this person for this role now. A history of sponsorship is not a policy, and policies, budgets and teams change.
When a title was sponsored. The sponsorship file has no filing years, so a matching title may be old.
Whether a sponsored title without a seniority word was an early-career hire. No marker is not proof.
Titles beyond the file's short 'top titles' list, and companies the file does not cover (it carries H-1B fields for about 5% of its rows and covers six states).
Whether the company in the file is the employer on the posting. The join behind the file has no published error rate.
Most of a posting's requirements. This version checks only minimum-experience lines; skills, tools, degree and every other line are listed for the person to read, not checked.

Whether the counted months are the kind of experience a line asks for ('in ML infra', 'using Python with ML frameworks'). The mode adds up the duration of every documented job; the kind is shown for a person to judge, never checked.
What the sponsorship numbers mean. 0.9 and 0.6 are declared screening assumptions, not chances of sponsorship, and approvals are company-wide, not ML-engineering approvals.

Employment type and hours. A job whose title doesn't say co-op, internship or similar is counted as employment of unstated type, never assumed full-time; assistantships, contract and fellowship work need supporting information before they count.

Whether co-op or internship time counts toward a stated minimum, or whether a 'required' line is enforced. Postings rarely say, so that becomes the question to ask; a posting can also soften its own requirements elsewhere in its text.
Whether the résumé file is complete. The mode counts only the experience the file lists, and cannot see a job listed anywhere else, such as a CV.
Anything about timeline or fit. Those numbers are declared by a person (or proposed by Claude Code), not measured.
Legal eligibility (OPT, STEM OPT, cap-gap). That is a question for the school's DSO or an attorney.
Whether applying works. For a discovered posting, 'available' means listed on its board and returned by its job endpoint at the time checked, nothing more.
What a computed timeline factor promises. It is a planning multiplier from declared dates and a declared time-to-start, not legal advice and not a forecast of any employer's hiring speed.
